routes.description: Establish that the universe’s origin and order, objective morality, evidence concerning Jesus, and religious experience cumulatively favor Christian theism, while showing that naturalistic evidence from evolution, suffering, and hiddenness does not reverse that comparison.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its independent and mutually reinforcing considerations warrant a transcendent personal God and connect that conclusion to Christian theism, with adequate answers to the principal naturalistic likelihood arguments.

motionBridge.description: The total evidence is more expected under Christian theism than under agnostic naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Cosmic beginning and life-permitting order require support for a transcendent personal creator and intelligent design.
Objective moral values and duties require an adequate foundation in God rather than an exclusively naturalistic ontology.
The historical case for Jesus’s resurrection must support divine action and authenticate distinctively Christian revelation.
Evolution, pain, tragedy, and hiddenness must be reconciled with Christian theism sufficiently to preserve the cumulative comparison.

subsidiaryBridges.description: The cause of a temporally finite universe must be connected defensibly to timelessness, immateriality, power, and personal agency.
Religious experience must provide defeasible warrant that coheres with the route’s independent arguments.

routes.description: Show cumulatively that major features of minds, life, suffering, moral behavior, and religious uncertainty are more probable under agnostic naturalism, while limiting the claimed force of cosmological, moral, resurrection, and experiential arguments for Christian theism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the comparative likelihood of the total evidence favors agnostic naturalism, or if the pro considerations remain too underdetermined to outweigh the naturalistic evidence without requiring a conclusive proof of naturalism.

motionBridge.description: The total evidence is more expected under agnostic naturalism than under Christian theism.

centralBridges.description: Each material fact must be compared by its relative probability under the rival worldviews and then incorporated cumulatively.
Evolution, mind-brain dependence, and the biological distribution of pain and pleasure must receive stronger expectations under naturalism.
Apparently uncompensated tragedy, absent divine comfort, and unclear religious revelation must count as evidence against Christian theism.
Cosmological, moral, resurrection, and experiential considerations must fail to supply a sufficient comparative advantage for Christian theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Objective moral truths and value must admit accounts that do not depend on grounding them in God’s nature.
Appeals to unknown goods, compensation, or compatibility must address comparative probability rather than mere logical consistency.

sections.title: Comparative probability and the cumulative burden
sections.rationale: Defines how multiple independent facts bear on the motion, including the distinction between showing evidence more likely on one worldview and conclusively proving that worldview.

sections.title: Cosmic origin, fine-tuning, and design
sections.rationale: Covers the universe’s beginning, causal explanation, inferred divine attributes, life-permitting conditions, and whether these facts favor personal design over naturalistic alternatives.

sections.title: Evolution, consciousness, and biological order
sections.rationale: Addresses evolutionary common descent, complex biological systems, mind-brain dependence, and pain-and-pleasure functions as competing evidence for design or naturalistic development.

sections.title: Morality, value, and human conduct
sections.rationale: Examines objective moral truth, possible divine and naturalistic grounds of value, moral disagreement, and the evidential significance of comparative moral behavior among believers.

sections.title: Jesus, revelation, and religious experience
sections.rationale: Tests the historical and inferential route from resurrection claims to divine authentication alongside experiential warrant, religious disagreement, and alternative interpretations.

sections.title: Suffering, divine comfort, and hiddenness
sections.rationale: Evaluates tragedy, biologically structured suffering, absent experiences of divine comfort, and proposed greater-good, doctrinal, compensatory, or epistemic explanations under the rival worldviews.
